_readme: Hand-written tasting data, merged into the sheet by scripts/migrate_sheet.py.
It lives here rather than in the spreadsheet so that re-running the migration
never destroys the work. Keyed on producer + wine, loosely matched, so small
edits to a name on the sheet won't orphan an entry.
body / sweetness / acidity / tannins are 1-10 and drive Find My Wine.
pairing is any of: just_drinking, cheese_charcuterie, seafood, hearty_meats.
short_desc is one line for the wine card; long_desc is 2-3 sentences for the
detail sheet. Both are written to be read by a guest, not a sommelier.
region / country are optional corrections — the Bubbles block in the original
sheet had 'Coonawarra, SA' filled down over Tasmanian and Italian producers.

wines.short_desc: Pure Grand Cru Chardonnay — green apple, lemon and a fine chalky finish.
wines.long_desc: Made entirely from Chardonnay grown on Grand Cru sites in the Côte des Blancs. Bright and precise, with orchard fruit, citrus zest and a faint brioche note from time on lees. The finish is dry and chalky, which makes it a natural with oysters and anything from the raw bar.

wines.short_desc: Roederer's modern blend — ripe pear, blood orange and a gentle smoky depth.
wines.long_desc: Built on the 2019 harvest with a large share of perpetual reserve wine, giving far more depth than the usual non-vintage. Wild peach and Williams pear meet blood orange and a soft, smoky note from oak-aged reserves. Dry at 7g/l dosage, with a supple mousse and a saline lift on the finish.

wines.short_desc: Pinot Noir from Grand Cru Bouzy — red-fruited, broad and quietly powerful.
wines.long_desc: A grower Champagne from Bouzy, where Pinot Noir ripens as well as anywhere in the region. Fuller and rounder than most non-vintage blends, with red berry fruit, a little baked apple and a savoury, almost meaty depth. Good with charcuterie and hard cheese rather than delicate food.

wines.wine: Cuvee Cuis 1er Cru Brut Blanc de Blancs
wines.short_desc: Taut, linear Chardonnay from Cuis — lemon, white flowers, chalk.
wines.long_desc: Gimonnet farm some of the best Chardonnay in the Côte des Blancs, and Cuis is their leanest, most mineral site. Very dry and tightly wound, with lemon pith, white blossom and a stony finish. One of the great aperitif Champagnes, and superb with raw fish.

wines.short_desc: Soft, generous and easy to like — white peach, honey and toast.
wines.long_desc: An approachable, fruit-forward style built for drinking rather than contemplating. White peach and pear with a touch of honey and toasted bread. Rounder and slightly softer than a classic dry Brut, which makes it an easy pour for a group.

wines.short_desc: The benchmark house style — pear, brioche and a famously silky mousse.
wines.long_desc: An equal blend of Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Meunier, aged far longer on lees than the appellation requires. Poached pear and white peach give way to brioche and toasted almond, all carried by a mousse so fine it's become the house's signature. Endlessly versatile — as good on its own as it is with food.

wines.short_desc: Fifty-year-old Chardonnay vines — stone fruit, almond, pink grapefruit.
wines.long_desc: A grower Champagne from Villers-Marmery, an unusual Chardonnay pocket in a corner of the Montagne de Reims better known for Pinot. Fruit from fifty-year-old vines gives real substance: tarte tatin, fresh almond and stone fruit, finishing on a burst of pink grapefruit.

wines.short_desc: Long-aged Premier Cru — baked apple, hazelnut and warm pastry.
wines.long_desc: Collet hold their wines on lees longer than most, and it shows in the texture. Baked apple and quince lead into hazelnut, honey and warm pastry, with the bubbles softened into something creamy rather than sharp. A Champagne for the table more than the aperitif.

wines.short_desc: Wild strawberry and redcurrant with a savoury, gently grippy finish.
wines.long_desc: A rosé with genuine Pinot character rather than just a blush of colour. Wild strawberry, redcurrant and a little blood orange, finishing dry and faintly savoury. Handles richer seafood — salmon, tuna, anything grilled — better than a white Champagne would.

wines.short_desc: Pinot-driven Aÿ grower — pear, white pepper and toasted brioche.
wines.long_desc: Eighty percent Pinot Noir from the Grand Cru village of Aÿ, and it drinks like it: broad, vinous and textured rather than crisp. Pear and peach with vanilla, white pepper and candied lemon, building through almond and brioche to a long, resonant finish. Serve it a touch warmer than you think.

wines.short_desc: A single fine year — citrus confit, hazelnut and real depth.
wines.long_desc: Only made in years Roederer judge worthy, and built around Pinot Noir from their own estate vineyards. Candied citrus and orchard fruit deepen into hazelnut and pastry with age, while the acidity stays taut underneath. Structured enough for a main course.

wines.short_desc: Bone-dry grower Champagne — citrus, orchard fruit and a saline snap.
wines.long_desc: An Extra Brut, meaning almost no dosage, so nothing is hidden behind sweetness. Lean and precise, with lemon, green orchard fruit and a distinctly saline finish. For drinkers who want their bubbles as dry as they come.

wines.short_desc: Single-vineyard and partly oaked — stone fruit, vanilla and toast.
wines.long_desc: Sourced entirely from the walled vineyard surrounding Taittinger's château at Pierry, with a portion vinified in oak. Richer and rounder than the house's standard cuvée: white stone fruit, vanilla, toasted nuts and a warm pastry note. A Champagne that wants food.

wines.short_desc: Estate Chardonnay from a single year — grapefruit, white flowers, chalk.
wines.long_desc: Chardonnay from Roederer's own parcels in the Côte des Blancs, made only in vintages that earn it. Grapefruit and white blossom over a firm chalky spine, with a creamy mid-palate from lees ageing. Precise, saline and long.

wines.short_desc: Grand Cru Chouilly at its most precise — lemon oil, oyster shell, chalk.
wines.long_desc: Special Club bottlings are a grower's best cuvée, submitted for peer tasting before release. This is Chardonnay at its most crystalline: lemon oil, green apple and an oyster-shell minerality that runs the length of the palate. Very dry, very long, and built to age.

wines.short_desc: Grand Cru Aÿ, Extra Brut — sweet almond, candied lemon, chalky spice.
wines.long_desc: Seventy percent Pinot Noir from Grand Cru Aÿ, partly fermented in cask and blocked from malolactic to keep the acidity bright. Sweet almond and candied lemon peel over a spicy, distinctly Aÿ character, with a chalky texture and a very mineral finish. Serious Champagne for the table.

wines.short_desc: All Meunier, and unusually savoury — orchard fruit, white pepper, chalk.
wines.long_desc: A rare single-variety Meunier from a house better known for restraint, and it's the boldest thing they make. Orchard fruit and pineapple lift into chamomile, sage and tangerine peel, then turn savoury with white pepper and a saline, faintly bitter finish. Drink it now rather than cellaring it.

wines.short_desc: The house's flagship — powerful and fine at once, built for the long haul.
wines.long_desc: Made in the style Churchill himself preferred: Pinot-dominant, full-bodied, but never heavy. Ripe orchard fruit and citrus confit sit over toasted hazelnut and pastry, with a mousse of remarkable finesse holding it all together. Extraordinary now and capable of another two decades.

wines.short_desc: Biodynamic estate fruit, silk-textured — citrus, white flowers, salt.
wines.long_desc: Drawn entirely from Roederer's biodynamically farmed Grand Cru parcels and held for years before release. The paradox of Cristal is weightlessness with intensity: citrus and white flowers, a creamy core, and a saline, chalky finish that goes on and on. Give it time in the glass.

wines.short_desc: Coonawarra Pinot Noir bubbles — red apple, strawberry and soft toast.
wines.long_desc: Made in the traditional method from estate Pinot Noir in Coonawarra. Red apple and strawberry with a gentle bready note from lees ageing, finishing soft and generous rather than austere. An easy, crowd-pleasing pour.

wines.short_desc: Yarra Chardonnay, light and citrusy with a soft creamy middle.
wines.long_desc: All Chardonnay from Soumah's Yarra Valley vineyards. Lemon and green apple with white blossom, and a creamy mid-palate that keeps it from feeling austere. Bright, uncomplicated and very drinkable as an aperitif.

wines.short_desc: Tasmanian sparkling — toasty brioche, citrus and crisp apple.
wines.long_desc: From the Coal River Valley in southern Tasmania, where the cool climate keeps acidity high. Lemon yellow with a fine bead, showing citrus and berry fruit alongside grilled nuts and brioche. Full and crisp, with a creamy structure and real length for the price.

wines.short_desc: Adelaide Hills classic blend — strawberry, citrus and fine bready lees.
wines.long_desc: The traditional Pinot Noir and Chardonnay pairing, grown high in the Adelaide Hills. Strawberry and citrus with a fine, persistent bead and a gentle bready note. Fresh and well balanced — a reliable house sparkling.

wines.short_desc: Tamar Valley bubbles — grapefruit, red apple and a nutty lees note.
wines.long_desc: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Holm Oak's vineyards in northern Tasmania's Tamar Valley. Grapefruit and red apple with a nutty, biscuity note from time on lees, and the crisp acidity Tasmania does so well. Clean, dry and food-friendly.

wines.short_desc: Cool-climate WA sparkling — lemon curd, almond meal and fine chalk.
wines.long_desc: Howard Park's traditional-method sparkling, given extended time on lees before disgorgement. Lemon curd and green apple with almond meal and a subtle toastiness, finishing dry and chalky. More serious than most Australian sparkling at this price.

wines.short_desc: Multi-vintage Tasmanian — nougat, stone fruit and a long saline finish.
wines.long_desc: Clover Hill's top multi-vintage release from Pipers River in northern Tasmania, blended across years for complexity. Nougat and stone fruit over a core of citrus, with a creamy texture from extended lees contact and a long, saline close. Handles richer seafood and soft cheese comfortably.

wines.short_desc: Margaret River Chardonnay and Pinot — white peach, citrus, fine mousse.
wines.long_desc: Vasse Felix's dedicated sparkling project, made from early-picked Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. White peach and citrus with a delicate floral lift and a fine, persistent mousse. Dry, precise and notably elegant for a young Australian sparkling.

wines.short_desc: Italy's answer to Champagne — green apple, white peach and toasted bread.
wines.long_desc: Franciacorta is made by the same method as Champagne, in Lombardy, and this is all Chardonnay. Green apple, citrus and white peach with delicate almond and fresh bread, then a creamy texture and vibrant acidity. Finishes clean with a mineral edge.

wines.short_desc: Five years on lees, barely any dosage — oyster shell, citrus, lemon blossom.
wines.long_desc: Single-vintage Tasmanian Chardonnay held a minimum of five years on lees with a very low 3g/l dosage, so nothing is softened. Crisp citrus opens into stone fruit and Delamere's signature oyster-shell minerality, with lemon blossom on the nose. Complex, bone-dry and remarkably long.

wines.wine: Bellavista Franciacorta Alma Gran Cuvee Brut
wines.short_desc: Franciacorta's benchmark — golden fruit, vanilla and a silky mousse.
wines.long_desc: Bellavista are one of Franciacorta's founding estates and Alma is their signature cuvée, blended across vintages with a portion barrel-fermented. Ripe golden orchard fruit and citrus meet vanilla, brioche and toasted nuts. Rich and rounded, with a soft, silky mousse.
